proposal.utterance: Classify 'an act of promising' in BFO terms.

entities.label: ActOfPromising
entities.rationale: An act of promising is a temporally extended happening — a speech act performed by an agent — that unfolds over time. It is not a continuant but an occurrent. Within BFO, Process (BFO_0000015) is the correct type: it is a bounded temporal event in which a promiser participates. It is modeled as a class (common noun kind) rather than an individual, since the utterance refers to the type 'an act of promising' generally.

relations.rationale: ActOfPromising is a subclass of Process (BFO_0000015), inheriting the character of a temporally unfolding occurrent.

open_questions: Should we also model the promissory obligation that results from the act? That would be a Role or Disposition (BFO_0000023 or BFO_0000016) inhering in the promiser after the act is completed.
Should ActOfPromising be further typed as a speech act or communicative process? If so, should it be placed under an intermediate class such as 'CommunicativeAct' (itself a subclass of BFO_0000015)?
Is the interest here in promising as a legal act (creating a LegalObligation) or as a general social/moral act? The answer affects what roles and dispositions are realized in the process.
Should the promisor and promisee be modeled as participants (via RO_0000057 has_participant) in this process class?
proposal.rationale_summary: An act of promising is most naturally classified in BFO as a Process (BFO_0000015): it is an occurrent that unfolds in time, has temporal boundaries (beginning and end of the promising speech act), and has participants (the promisor and, typically, a promisee). It is not a continuant because it does not persist by being wholly present at every moment — it is completed. It is not a Quality or Role, though it may realize a Disposition (e.g., the capacity to make binding commitments) and may bring about a Role (e.g., the role of being obligated). The utterance 'an act of promising' uses a common noun, so ActOfPromising is minted as a class, subclass of BFO_0000015. No existing working-ontology class covers this kind precisely, so a new class is proposed.
